html:
Porfirio Díaz was a Mexican general who ruled Mexico as president, with one break, from 1876 to 1911. His long rule, the Porfiriato, ended in the Mexican Revolution.

A hero of the war against the French at Puebla, he took power in a revolt in 1876, promising no re-election, and then had himself re-elected again and again. Under the motto order and progress, he brought peace, railways, mines, oil wells and factories, much of them owned by American and British investors. A group of advisers, the científicos, ran the economy.

Peasant villages lost their lands to great estates, workers who struck were shot, and the press was muzzled. In 1910 he claimed victory in a rigged election against Francisco Madero, who called for revolt. The Mexican Revolution forced Díaz into exile in 1911. He died in Paris. He made modern Mexico, and the anger that remade it in the Constitution of 1917.
